rich_summary: After Drona’s death, his son Ashwatthama burns with grief and shame, declaring that he will annihilate the Panchalas to repay the debt he owes his slain father. In a fierce speech to the Kauravas, he condemns his own strength and weapons for failing to protect Drona and vows terrible vengeance. He reveals the secret of the Narayana weapon, a divine missile granted to Drona by Lord Narayana with strict conditions: it is unstoppable and must not be used rashly or against defenseless foes. Determined to unleash it, Ashwatthama invokes the weapon. Terrifying cosmic omens follow—winds rage, mountains split, rivers reverse, and darkness spreads—striking fear in gods and warriors alike. As the Kaurava army rallies around him, the Pandavas prepare to respond to the catastrophic divine weapon now unleashed upon the battlefield.

highlight_spans.why: Ashwatthama’s opening vow to destroy the Panchalas sets the emotional and narrative stakes of the episode.
His anguished cry condemning his own weapons and prowess reveals the depth of his grief over Drona’s humiliation and death.
The warning about the Narayana weapon explains its divine nature and the ethical limits placed on its use.
The moment Ashwatthama invokes the Narayana weapon marks the decisive turning point of the chapter.
The cosmic disturbances—winds, trembling earth, and reversed rivers—dramatically signal the arrival of a catastrophic divine force.

top_scenes.scene_text: Ashwatthama standing in his chariot with blazing fury, raising his weapon to invoke the Narayana astra while the Kaurava army roars behind him.
The Narayana weapon awakening as dark winds howl, lightning cracks across a cloudless sky, mountains split, and the battlefield trembles.
Terrified warriors and kings looking upward as unnatural darkness spreads and rivers reverse while ominous creatures gather over the battlefield.
